rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 1 line 23 'The reasons for personal-first land in Phase 3' — a forward pointer, but it names the destination explicitly (Phase 3, which exists at chunk 5) rather than assuming unestablished info now; harm (an unresolvable referent) is absent, this is a signpost not a dangling antecedent. All other referents ('the skill', 'the grade', 'the reasons') resolve against chunk 0's H1/lede or an earlier same-file chunk (e.g. chunk 5 line 74 'wrote it there in Phase 1' resolves against chunk 1; 'Phase 2's invoke-and-critique' resolves against chunk 3).

No 'the opening lecture said' style backward callback to another file anywhere in the body. Closest candidate: chunk 7 line 87 'Module 4 reads this skill' — a forward pointer named by module number, not a positional callback into another file's content, and not something the reader needs to resolve now.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 5 line 74 references 'Phase 1' and, via 'the invoke-and-critique' (chunk 6 line 79 restates it as Phase 2's), both exist as headings in this same file (chunk 1, chunk 3). No dead-beat references found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File contains no guess-before-reveal / predict-then-watch instruction anywhere in the body; rule doesn't apply to this exercise's beat shape.

Closest candidate: chunk 2 (lines 39-43, 'Answer from how your codebase really tests'), the shortest non-title chunk — but it carries two self-contained instructive bullets (concrete good-answer example + push-back move), not a wait-state. Every chunk carries a standalone claim.

Checked all 7 non-title headers against their chunk content: e.g. chunk 6 'Decide if it graduates to the team' (line 76) is followed by exactly a graduation decision (team-PR conversation, personal-as-fine-final-home); chunk 4 'Sharpen the skill from what came back' (line 62) is followed by the self-critique/re-invoke content. No header contradicted by its own chunk.

Checked all 5 sub-items across all chunks: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction found; no anaphora/epistrophe triples found; no self-grading superlatives (closest: chunk 0 line 11 'test strategy authored generically is a pyramid diagram' — a claim about the failure mode, not self-praise of this exercise); no number-with-retraction pattern found (file has no hedged numbers); no verb triplets with an empty leg found. Sub-item 'same-window self-charity' (chunk 4 line 65) is a coined descriptive handle naming a real mechanism (invoke-then-grade in one context window), not a vague abstraction-noun stack.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 7 'What this sets up' (line 85): neither imperative ('Ship the skill...') nor a Phase-label, and not a declarative claim either (it doesn't assert a proposition the way 'Passing is not proof' does) — it's a topic-label noun phrase, a shape the rule's letter doesn't name a home for. Harm check: this doesn't dilute the rare-declaration convention (rule 15's actual concern) since it never poses as a declaration, and the same exact heading appears in curriculum/exercises/map-the-access-surface.md:93, suggesting a deliberate closer-section convention rather than a slip. Filing as a rule question for the maintainer, not a comprehension defect: does check_slides.md §15 need a third bucket for forward-look/closer topic-labels, or should this heading be reworded to an imperative ('See what this sets up' / phase-label)?
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either add a topic-label carve-out to §15 for forward-look closer sections (citing this file + map-the-access-surface.md as the pattern), or reword the heading to an imperative.
